institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nature and the activities surrounding that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Going on exchange was the best decision I ever made during law school.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UiT has a very informative website, where you can find every piece of information you need. It might take some time, but the information is there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You receive a lot of information during the Debut Week for International students, which I recommend you participate in. At least the social gatherings at first, not all the things during the debut week was that important, and if you meet a group of people that want to skip some of the information lectures that does have any important information, then just do that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was a bit difficult to find housing. Firstly, I had applied through my host institution, but apparently something went wrong, and even though I had applied and got a confirmation of application, however they did not look at my application. Therefore, make sure your application makes it all the way through.
Regarding private housing, I looked on
Finn.no
and
Hybel.no
. It was quite challenging to find housing that offered short term rent. However, after sending approximately 20 applications, I got a very nice place in town.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Regarding private housing, I looked on
Finn.no
and
Hybel.no
. It was quite challenging to find housing that offered short term rent. However, after sending approximately 20 applications, I got a very nice place in town.
Private housing tends to be a bit more expansive than that offered through the host institution, but you do get more for your money in private housing. The places tend to be bigger and have more facilities like a living room etc. Furthermore, I lived with three Norwegians, which where a very nice way to learn the language and offered good opportunities to make friends besides those on exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The entire process tends to be very bureaucratic and takes a lot of time. You need to send a lot of documents and such back and forth from your home university and to the host university. Furthermore, the final approval for your stay might come a little late as was the course selection a bit late regarding when you leave for the exchange. But all is taken care of before you arrive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UiT's webpage.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got both the classes I had signed up for. Though, I initially thought I could take other classes, which were part of my decision to go I later found out those classes where only for a special program that exchange students couldn't take. Otherwise, the process of reregistering for classes was straightforward.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was a bit lower than at KU. Additionally, it did not feel like 15 ECTS point courses. The workload was smaller, and the courses are structured after a block structure. So, you only have classes and lectures in the courses for a certain number of weeks. The courses do not have classes during the entire semester. Though exams are still at the end of the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Because the classes are way smaller and not as many students attend so it is very interactive. It is more personal in a way, and everyone can participate more. They do have questions for the classes, as we do at KU, that you need to prepare before class –depending on the course you take.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: JUR-3050 General Law of the Sea and JUR-3626 International Criminal Law, Atrocity Crimes, and Transitional Justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: JUR-3050 General Law of the Sea. It complements the surroundings of your stay, and you can draw a lot of connections. Furthermore, UiT has an entire department for like Law of the Sea, so they are very skilled in that legal field.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Because of the private housing situation I had to buy pillows, duvets and sheets.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The books were a bit more expansive then first imagined. However, qua the Norwegian kroner being less worth than the Danish at the time of my exchange, you saved a lot when buying groceries etc. Furthermore, they had a lot of student discount in different places, which made it possible to do a lot of activities for example use the sauna, go to yoga classes, join the gym etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different activities you could join. UiT were also very good at informing about every event held a school as well as in town. You received an email every other week with information regarding activities you could join. I for example enjoyed the knitting club for international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you enjoy knitting or want to learn, like I did, you should join that. Otherwise, join a gym or just participate in what you can. There is something for everyone.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I truly recommend going hiking and exploring the nearby nature. This was a major aspect of my trip, and it made it very unforgettable. I enjoyed hiking during the summer and skiing during the winter. You can rent free gear through Turbu or pay for rent though Tromsø Outdoor. Either way, there is excellent opportunities for renting what you might need. The busses connect the entire island and takes you basically everywhere. See and explore the place every time you have the chance!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. You get a hang of the language quick, and the culture is not that different from what you are used to. Naturally, there are some differences, but generally everyone is just very friendly and welcoming. You kind of feel welcome from the moment you arrive.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to find them during activities or other social gatherings where it is easier to meet them. You don't meet a lot during your classes, because it is primarily made up of international students. But otherwise just talk to them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing. There were no big challenges.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and open mindedness. Everyone was so sweet and always wanted to help etc. Furthermore, I loved their approach to everyday life. Everything is centered around their life outside of works, which means they adapt their working hours to fit, what they want to do. You could meet locals on top of mountains at 12 on a Tuesday. This balance between work and private life, was very enlightening. They just have a more chill approach to life and especially work life balance.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.	Enjoy the activities UiT has to offer 
2.	Explore nature 
3.	Adjust your expectations for the academic level (just a different way than at KU)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UiT is extremely big, so familiarize yourself with the app MazeMap.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of the exchange was defiantly the experience of a chill everyday life. From the courses to your free time, everything is just less stressful. You get to really work with the courses and the textbooks, because there is not as much to read and work with, so you have the time to read everything. Furthermore, you do not have a lot of classes, so lots of time to explore the nature, which where an equally great experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There were not that many great challenges. You just have to adopt to a new way of life, but when you have landed and start to have routines you really fall into place.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I highly recommend an exchange in Tromsø.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
